name: Urban Feline Perspective

scraped_sources.title: Feral cat
scraped_sources.description: Unowned or untamed domestic cat in the outdoors
scraped_sources.extract: A feral cat or stray cat is an unowned domestic cat that lives freely outdoors and avoids human contact; it does not allow itself to be handled or touched, and usually remains hidden from humans. Feral cats may breed over dozens of generations and become a mesopredator or even a local apex predator in urban, savannah and bushland environments, especially on islands where native animals did not evolve alongside natural predators. Some feral cats may become more comfortable with people who regularly feed them, but even with long-term attempts at socialization, they usually remain aloof and are most active after dusk. Of the 700 million cats in the world, an estimated 480 million are feral.

scraped_sources.title: Cat senses
scraped_sources.extract: Cat senses are adaptations that allow cats to be highly efficient predators. Cats are good at detecting movement in low light, have an acute sense of hearing and smell, and their sense of touch is enhanced by long whiskers that protrude from their heads and bodies. These senses evolved to allow cats to hunt effectively at dawn and dusk.

scraped_sources.title: Cat behavior
scraped_sources.extract: Cat behavior encompasses the actions and reactions displayed by a cat in response to various stimuli and events. Cat behavior includes body language, elimination habits, aggression, play, communication, hunting, grooming, urine marking, and face rubbing. It varies among individuals, colonies, and breeds.

environment: a narrow cobblestone alley flanked by damp brick walls and overflowing wooden crates
a dizzying zinc rooftop slick with twilight drizzle and chimney smoke
the sheltered hollow beneath a market stall smelling of salt herring and sawdust
a sun-warmed windowsill overlooking the restless bustle of the street below
hazards: a snarling neighborhood dog straining against a rusted wire chain
a sudden downpour cascading off gutters and flooding the cobblestones
a territory-marking rival tomcat bristling on the garden fence
an impatient street vendor wielding a wooden broom
dialogue_templates: Across the yard, {name} lowers its ears flat and emits a warning rasp: the alley has already been claimed.
From the open doorway, {name} tosses a scrap of warm fat into the sawdust with a quiet whistle.
The low, vibrating rumble of {name} rattles against the wooden fence: one step closer means teeth.
sensory_details: the damp scent of moss, chimney soot, and frying lard riding the evening breeze
the sharp prickle of cold rain striking your ears as whiskers twitch with vigilance
the silent, cushioned impact of your paws springing between wet stone steps
every distant footstep vibrating through the floorboards into your ribcage
